hints: The crate moves with constant speed along the horizontal surface.
Divide $12\text{ m}$ by $8\text{ s}$ to determine the constant speed.
walkthrough:
Calculate the constant speed from the given distance and time:
$$v = \frac{d}{t} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The crate moves in a straight line at a constant speed, meaning there is no acceleration ($a = 0$).

Step 1: Use the standard definition of constant speed:
$$v = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$$

Step 2: Substitute the distance $d = 12\text{ m}$ and time $t = 8\text{ s}$:
$$v = \frac{12}{8} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: The force of magnitude $25\text{ N}$ acts at an angle of $20^\circ$ above the horizontal direction of displacement.
Use the work done formula for a constant force inclined at angle $\theta$: $W = F d \cos \theta$.
Evaluate $25 \times 12 \times \cos 20^\circ$ and round to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Calculate the work done by the $25\text{ N}$ force along the horizontal displacement of $12\text{ m}$:
$$W = F d \cos \theta = 25 \times 12 \times \cos 20^\circ = 300 \cos 20^\circ \approx 281.9\text{ J} \approx 282\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the components of the pulling force along the direction of motion:
The force has magnitude $F = 25\text{ N}$ and is inclined at $\theta = 20^\circ$ above the horizontal. The component of this force parallel to the horizontal surface is:
$$F_x = F \cos 20^\circ = 25 \cos 20^\circ$$

Step 2: Calculate the work done over distance $d = 12\text{ m}$:
$$W = F_x \times d = (25 \cos 20^\circ) \times 12 = 300 \cos 20^\circ$$

Step 3: Perform the numerical evaluation:
$$\cos 20^\circ \approx 0.9396926$$
$$W \approx 300 \times 0.9396926 = 281.908\text{ J} \approx 282\text{ J}$$

hints: Power is the rate of doing work: $P = \frac{W}{t}$.
Divide your answer from part (b) by the duration $8\text{ s}$, or use $P = F v \cos 20^\circ$ with $v = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate $\frac{281.9}{8}$ to obtain the power in watts.
walkthrough:
Calculate the power at which the force is working:
$$P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{281.91}{8} \approx 35.2\text{ W}$$
$$\text{Alternatively: } P = (25 \cos 20^\circ) \times 1.5 = 37.5 \cos 20^\circ \approx 35.2\text{ W}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Method 1: Using work done divided by time.
Power is defined as the work done per unit time:
$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$
From part (b), the unrounded work done is $W = 300 \cos 20^\circ \approx 281.908\text{ J}$, and the time taken is $t = 8\text{ s}$:
$$P = \frac{281.908}{8} \approx 35.2385\text{ W} \approx 35.2\text{ W}$$

Method 2: Using horizontal force times speed.
The forward component of the pulling force is $F_{\parallel} = 25 \cos 20^\circ$, and from part (a) the constant speed is $v = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = F_{\parallel} \times v = (25 \cos 20^\circ) \times 1.5 = 37.5 \cos 20^\circ \approx 35.2\text{ W}$$
